facts.text: Maryville was incorporated July 11 1795 and named for Mary Grainger Blount, wife of territorial governor William Blount.
The town’s earliest settlement was Fort Craig, a wooden palisade built by Revolutionary War veteran John Craig in 1785, which later became the site of Maryville.
Downtown Maryville’s historic Park Theatre, one of three early theaters, still stands on Broadway Ave and reflects the town’s early 20th‑century cultural life.
In 1995, a bicentennial timeline was compiled by David Morton, linking Maryville’s local history to national and world events.
The former WA Dunlap Building, erected around 1910, housed Bogle McCammon Furniture Co. and now serves as a reminder of Maryville’s commercial past.
